result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

My overall recommendation is **1Password if ease of use and team collaboration matter most; Bitwarden if keeping costs down is the priority.**

A business password manager is worth paying for because it gives you secure shared credentials, individual employee accounts, access controls, and the ability to revoke access when someone leaves.

## My top 4 choices

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

- Very easy for employees to use.
- Shared vaults for departments and projects.
- Excellent access permissions and admin controls.
- Security monitoring and password health reports.
- Canadian company, headquartered in Toronto.

**Price\:** Teams Starter Pack around C\$29.95/month for up to 10 users, billed annually.

Website: [1Password Business](https://1password.com/business)

---

![The best password managers in 2026 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/NzVuMgIchg5mHs-Kr9143cu9YVcLD78U-cfqnnpzpdksR6kB5LPVR6OyqUe0J0PAWilFgVX5RafeZ-AzNa_G6WUPgI8J1U4oAahEfqnQQL2SaxhVwFg9jy1o1kVewXMyq40iQ1cCkpkzpsh_DQntfgs6e3PLRpQFbO3dRcV-HQGbTSkVwYxuDvCJM657Aw6_?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Excellent pricing.
- Open-source platform.
- Shared collections and team management.
- Strong security and administration features.
- Self-hosting options.

**Price\:** Approximately US\$4/user/month for Teams, billed annually.

Website: [Bitwarden Business](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Good administrative controls.
- Shared team folders.
- Strong security and compliance features.
- Useful for businesses with more complex access requirements.

**Price\:** Business Starter around US\$2/user/month, billed annually.

Website: [Keeper Business](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused.
- End-to-end encryption.
- Secure sharing.
- Good option for teams already using Proton services.

**Price\:** Business plans start around US\$1.99/user/month.

Website: [Proton Pass for Business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

[www.northvetted.ca](https://www.northvetted.ca/reviews/best-password-manager-canada?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[technovapartners.com](https://technovapartners.com/en/insights/best-business-password-managers-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for in a small business

Regardless of which one you choose, make sure it has\:

1. Shared vaults – employees can access company credentials without sharing passwords through email or chat.
2. Individual accounts – everyone has their own login.
3. Access management – revoke an employee's access immediately when they leave.
4. Two-factor authentication (2FA).
5. Audit logs – see who accessed or changed shared credentials.
6. Secure sharing – share credentials without exposing them in plain text.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I'd like to help you pick the right one rather than have you pay for features you don't need.

**1\. How many people will use it?**

- 2–5
- 6–10
- 11–25
- 25–50

**2\. What kind of business is it?**

- General office / administration
- IT / software development
- Construction / trades
- Professional services
- Other

**3\. What's most important?**

- Lowest possible cost
- Best security
- Easiest for employees to use
- Strong administrative control and shared passwords

With those answers, I can narrow it down to one recommendation and estimate what it would cost your team in Canadian dollars.
